question.problem: Consider the data sets $x$ and $y$ such that $\text{Cov}(x,y)=-8$ and their standard deviations are ${\sigma }_{x}=3$ and ${\sigma }_{y}=4.$ Compute the corresponding linear correlation coefficient. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The (population) linear correlation coefficient for data sets $x$ and $y$ is given by the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho (x,y) & =\frac{\text{Cov}(x,y)}{{\sigma }_{x}\cdot {\sigma }_{y}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting our numbers, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho (x,y) & =\frac{(-8)}{3\cdot 4} \\  & ≈-0.67\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
